game: ATL @ NO, Week 12 2025, kickoff 2025-11-23 16:25 ET, Caesars-week pack line NO -1.5 / total 41.5, roof dome

script.base: Morning-of-kickoff read from the pack only: dome, NO -1.5, total 41.5, implied NO 21.5 / ATL 20.0. Not a blowout and not a shootout. Both teams stay in it, so starter snaps should hold. NO's tilt is pass-leaning rather than a Kamara clock-grind because Alvin Kamara is questionable (ankle), Brandin Cooks is out, and Tyler Shough is the only NO QB in the weeks 8-10 rush log (5 carries). Targets in that window already concentrate on Chris Olave (24), Rashid Shaheed (21) and Juwan Johnson (16). ATL, with Drake London out, is more Bijan Robinson on the ground (52 carries, 234 rush yards in weeks 9-11) plus short throws than a London shot profile. A 21.5 team total can still clear a 50.5 TE line and a 58.5 WR line; it cannot carry a full both-teams overs stack.
script.flip1: NO leads early, Taliese Fuaga plays, and Kamara (or Taysom Hill 13/56 and Devin Neal 7/33 if Kamara is limited) runs out the clock into an ATL rush defense that allows 4.89 YPC and 33 runs of 10+. ATL (Michael Penix 3 rushes and Kirk Cousins 1 rush both show up in weeks 9-11; starter not named) falls behind and abandons Bijan's carry rate. Olave and Johnson late volume stalls; Bijan rush yards die.
script.flip2: Bijan's last two rush lines (84 and 104) plus NO's ankle/tackle issues (Kamara questionable, Fuaga questionable, Barry Wesley out) push Shough into a chase. Olave (320 air yards on 24 targets) and Johnson (176 yards on 16 targets) both clear, and Shaheed (143 yards, no prop on the board) joins them. ATL's 44% blitz either feeds Johnson or, if it actually gets home, kills Olave's deep yards. A true shootout is the less likely version of this flip under a 41.5 total.

injury_fallout: Known out before kickoff (nflverse injury report in the pack; inactives ~90 minutes prior are not in the pack): ATL WR Drake London out (knee) vacates the weeks 9-11 lead role of 31 targets, 341 yards and 334 air yards. Same-side absorbers already on the field in that window are Darnell Mooney (17 targets, only 66 yards, 241 air), Kyle Pitts (15/90/175), Bijan Robinson (17/93/40), David Sills (4/11/55) and Charlie Woerner (1/14/5). Casey Washington is on the prop board (recyds 19.5, last4 19/0/17/25) but is absent from the weeks 9-11 target list, so he is not the documented next man. ATL also out: CB Billy Bowman Jr. (Achilles), LB Josh Woods (hamstring), LB Malik Verdon (shoulder), DT Zach Harrison (knee). Questionable, unresolved: LB Leonard Floyd (hamstring), G Chris Lindstrom (foot), G Matthew Bergeron (ankle). If both guards sit, ATL pressure allowed rises, rushing efficiency falls, and quick throws (Pitts, Bijan) beat deep Mooney. NO out: WR Brandin Cooks (personal; only 7 targets and 38 yards in weeks 8-10, a small ~8% share of the 91 listed targets) and T Barry Wesley (hip). NO questionable: RB Alvin Kamara (ankle), T Taliese Fuaga (ankle). Kamara is not out, so Kendre Miller (last4 rush 65/41/21/7, line 24.5) is a conditional sleeper only, not a confirmed handoff. No snap or rep limits are listed.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone charting are not in the pack, so shell is uncalled. Location splits over 10 games are the proxy: NO allows YPA left 6.8 (125 throws), middle 8.1 (49), right 7.68 (108). ATL allows left 7.69 (111), middle 10.49 (57), right 5.69 (114). ATL's right side is the coverage strength; the middle is the bleed.
matchup.pressure: NO blitz rate 35%. ATL EPA/dropback is -0.23 vs the blitz and +0.08 with no blitz, so NO pressure is a real problem for whichever of Penix or Cousins plays and should force quicker throws. ATL blitz rate 44%. NO EPA/dropback is -0.07 vs the blitz and -0.10 with no blitz, so the blitz does not uniquely collapse NO, but both splits are negative. Pressure rate (as opposed to blitz rate) is not in the pack. ATL guards Lindstrom and Bergeron questionable would add ATL pressure allowed if they sit. NO protection is already thin: Wesley out, Fuaga questionable.
matchup.bleeds: ATL bleeds the middle (10.49 YPA on 57 throws), explosives (28 passes of 20+ for 316 yards) and the run (4.89 YPC, 33 runs of 10+). NO is not a run bleed (4.23 YPC, 33 runs of 10+) and has only 25 passes of 20+ for 303 yards in 10 games. Missing ATL coverage bodies that matter today: Bowman Jr., Woods, Verdon. Harrison (DT) out also softens the front that already allows 4.89 YPC.
matchup.overlap: Cleanest overlap is Juwan Johnson (16 targets, 176 yards, 157 air yards in weeks 8-10) into ATL's middle and the two out linebackers, in a 44% blitz environment that funnels to tight ends. Olave (24 targets, 224 yards, 320 air) overlaps the explosive-pass allowance and a secondary missing Bowman, but 320 air yards is the profile that dies if the 44% blitz gets home, and ATL's right side (5.69 YPA) is not a bleed if that is where he aligns. Alignment is not charted. ATL's own overlap, London's 31 targets into a NO defense that is not bleeding (middle 8.1 YPA, 25 explosives), is real usage news but a worse defensive spot, which is why no ATL pass leg is on the card.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the Johnson over lost. The 10.49 middle YPA was 57 throws of noise, Woods and Verdon were not the tight-end coverage backs, and Floyd either played or was never that defender. Kamara's ankle held, ATL's 4.89 YPC front (Harrison already out) was the easy path, and Shough's negative EPA splits (-0.07 vs blitz, -0.10 without) showed up as a 17-point grind where Johnson repeated the 31-yard game. Olave lost the same Monday for a different reason: the 44% blitz finally got home behind Wesley out and Fuaga limited, the 320 air yards became empty, Shaheed's 21-target share took the first read, and Olave landed on 57 against a number that was only a season median, not a soft book line. If that counter is the one the human believes, the lean Olave leg is the one to cut; the Johnson read is still the cleaner overlap, but it is not a bet without a real price.
slip_story: One story only: competitive dome game, NO pass concentration with Kamara's ankle a tilt not a requirement, ATL linebackers and Bowman out. Two-leg same-script stack, no touchdowns, one market per player: Johnson recyds over 50.5 with Olave recyds over 58.5. They can both clear inside a 21.5 team total if the yards sit on those two rather than on Shaheed. Do not add ATL overs (Pitts, Mooney, Bijan) — that needs the other team's points and fights the 41.5 total. Do not add a total under. Do not add Miller or Kamara; those need the opposite run script and an inactive list we do not have. Not a ticket to place.
